master_zero: Audio sync event at master time T = 0. All t_in/t_out below are master time; the renderer derives each source timecode as src = T + offset(camera), reading offsets from out/sync_report.json so the EDL never has to be rewritten if the offsets are re-measured.

cameras.cam1: front left, medium wide on stage
cameras.cam3: wide back, full stage and audience
cameras.cam4: side angle, wide with audience foreground

audio.gain_note: Cameras 1 and 2 peak at 0.0 dBFS in the original recordings - the drums overloaded the camera microphones before we ever touched the footage, and that clipping cannot be undone. This 0.85 (about -1.4 dB) keeps headroom so the AAC encoder does not add further distortion on top, and brings the integrated loudness closer to the -14 LUFS streaming target.

bed.note: Camera 1 is the only source spanning the whole body, so it carries the continuous bed. A single bed means no cut ever produces an audio discontinuity.

overrides.reason: Camera 2 sits closest to the drums, so its audio is used across the drum section. Crossfaded in and out because the clips are frame-aligned, so no phase artefact occurs. Set enabled=false to fall back to the Camera 1 bed alone.

lines: Edited from a machine-readable Editing Decision List
Every editing decision was reviewed and approved by a human editor.
This is a semi-automated pipeline, not full automation.
Footage processed entirely offline. No video was uploaded to any cloud service.
Recorded and shared with the consent of participants and guardians.

segments.reason: Wide back camera establishes the full stage, the audience and the scale of the hall before any close work.
Front-left camera is tighter on the group choreography, so the movement reads clearly after the wide establishing shot.
Side angle puts the audience in the foreground, showing the performance in its setting rather than in isolation.
Return to front-left for the synchronised arm sequence, which is the best-framed moment of the opening routine.
Wide back camera captures the whole formation as the group spreads across the stage.
Front-left covers the handover from the opening routine into the drum section. Crossfade marks the change of section.
Camera 2 is the only close framing available. It carries the drum performance where facial expression is the content.
Cut wide to re-establish the full drum line, so the close-ups do not lose the audience's sense of the whole group.
Back to the close framing for the strongest passage of the drum routine.
Front-left shows the full drum line head on as the routine builds to its finish.
Final close framing on the performers. Camera 2 stops recording at T = 43.05, so this is the last close-up the footage allows.

Wide back camera for the closing moment. The performance ends at about T = +43.5 and the hall lights drop immediately after, so the cut stops here rather than running on into the slide presentation that follows. Camera 3 is the only wide still recording at this point. Crossfade closes the sequence rather than cutting hard to the credits.
